To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Pruning neural networks at initialization can be done more effectively by randomly shuffling or sampling new initializations, and that this property is a consequence of the underlying heuristics and the desire to prune early in training.

(i) the accuracy of SNIP, GraSP, SynFlow, and random pruning at initialization can be improved by randomly shuffling the pruned weights, and (ii) these methods are outperformed by magnitude pruning after training.
(1) pruning at initialization can be more effective than pruning after training; and (2) recent methods for pruning at initialization are missing the mark.

the fundamental question of whether pruning at initialization can achieve the performance of pruning after training, a question we answer negatively.

the following questions: (1) Can pruning at initialization be improved? (2) What are the challenges in pruning at initialization? (3) What can be done to improve pruning at initialization?
